title.narrative: Provision of immediate life-saving emergency food assistance for the flood-affected populations in Beletweyne district through Unconditional Cash transfers

description.narrative:
ltpgtThe proposed project seeks to improve access to basic food items for 810 households or 4860 vulnerable men, women, girls, and boys including 15% of people with disabilities and marginalized communities who are food insecure and their condition could be worse in the coming El Nino if not addressed. The project is designed to address the immediate food needs of the most vulnerable rural households from villages under Beletweyne district through unconditional cash transfers valued at USD70/hh to cover the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB). The project will primarily target riverine communities that were affected by recent floods in 2023 and are expected to be the most hit by the predicted El Nino floods. lt/pgtltpgtThe project will be implemented in a period of 4 months in the proposed 18 villages of (Dolamadow, Qarsoni, Labka, Haracadey, Dolagal, Hodley, Helakelyo, Garaash, Lafole, Dheriyow, Qoqane, Biyoqurun, Kurtumaley, Bacadbuke, Lugbari, Dabeyl, Bulakahin and Silgalow). The proposed villages fall under our ongoing food security intervention areas where we are providing farm inputs, distribution of tools, and drums, land preparation community training on GAPs, Farm Management, DRR, Organic Fertilizer, and Financial Management. The ongoing project is funded by ltbgtBMZlt/bgt through our partner ltbgtaction medeorlt/bgt based in Germany. The project will undertake beneficiary registration, agreement signing with a mobile transfer company, transfer of cash to the 810 hhs, and a Post post-distribution monitoring activity to verify beneficiaries' satisfaction and get feedback. The organization will implement the project directly, and the targeting of eligible households will be undertaken jointly with community-based committees in each location using an inclusive community-based target (ICBT) approach that is participatory. WARDI will work closely with IRW to avoid overlap of activities in the same villages. Also on matters of water provision to affected populations, WARDI will work with Action Aid and AADSOM. Vulnerable groups such as people with disabilities and the older population will be integrated into the program in close work relationships with MCAN. Other partners with whom WARDI will work closely will include HINNA on the provision of NFI kits and plastic sheets, and HIWA on protection issues of the affected persons. ltbrgtlt/pgt
